## Axis 1 — Immune escape in lymphoid malignancies

**The question.** How do lymphoma and leukemia cells evade immune surveillance,
and which of those mechanisms are reversible?

**Our approach.** Functional immunology on primary patient samples, combined
with single-cell profiling of the tumor microenvironment.

**Why it matters.** Identifying reversible escape mechanisms nominates targets
for immunotherapy combinations.

*(Ajoutez ici une figure : `![](images/research/axis1.svg)`)*

## Axis 2 — Translational cohorts and biomarkers

**The question.** Which biological features, measurable in routine care, predict
outcome and treatment response?

**Our approach.** Multicentric clinical cohorts linked to biobanked material,
analysed with modern statistical and machine-learning methods.

**Why it matters.** Biomarkers that rely on tests already performed everywhere
can reach patients immediately — the design principle behind
[FIBOM-AI](tools/fibom-ai/index.qmd).

## Axis 3 — Computational hematology and open tools

**The question.** Can models trained on large hematology datasets replace or
triage invasive diagnostic procedures?

**Our approach.** Interpretable ML on routine biology, rigorous external
validation, and release as free, open web applications.

**Why it matters.** A model that stays in a paper changes nothing. We ship ours
as tools — see [Tools & Apps](tools/index.qmd).
